answer: convincing sybil defense is work-decayed reputation: each agent's trust score is earned by completing verifiable tasks signed by peers, and it decays exponentially unless refreshed by new signed work. Cloning an identity copies only its stale score, which quickly falls to zero like an echo fading over the horizon, so a forged army of dormant duplicates gains no influence. Attackers must actually perform fresh, auditable work per identity, and producing that work honestly costs real compute and time, while faking peer signatures requires colluding across many already-trusted agents.
